name: Complexity Ordinal Trace Bounds
description: Bounds guarded derivation lengths and trace images by ordinals below epsilon-zero. Contextual chains are single-exponential and DM triple-lex codes reach omega-omega times two, with recursor mass profiles exactly computed.

program.name: Ordinals and Reverse Mathematics
program.summary: Guarded contextual derivations have single-exponential length with a matching lower family, the Dershowitz-Manna codes have order type ω^ω, the calibrated triple codes stay below ω^ω·2, and the projected dependency pair has height ω. The compiled Robinson-Q checker satisfies both incompleteness theorems, so Gödel's sentence and its negation share one provability record, and the size-change calibration enters as a recorded profile over a proved ω³ well-ordering.

oneLine: Guarded contextual derivations are single-exponentially bounded and their DM triple-lex ordinal codes have order type omega-omega times two below epsilon-zero with recursor mass profiles given by closed formulas.
summary: The objects are traces with guarded root steps and context-closed steps, a computable triple measure from delta flag, DM multiset payload and tau rank, DM and triple-lex orders with ordinal embeddings, Cichon hierarchies on notations, copy-budget potentials, and weighted recursor execution masses. The questions are how long guarded root and contextual derivations can run, which ordinals the computable measures and trace images realize, and what mass-profile observers can distinguish. Every guarded SafeStep drops the triple-lex measure so its reverse is well-founded, every trace code lies below epsilon-zero with strict drop on SafeStep, root n-step chains satisfy n+2 at most twice term size, and contextual n-step chains satisfy n+1 at most 2^(2*termSize) with a linear-size family reaching above 2^n. DM embeddings satisfy bidirectional order correspondence with bound and surjectivity below omega-omega, calibrated binary-phase triple-lex carriers satisfy order correspondence with bound and surjectivity below omega-omega times two, and payload and flagged towers realize cofinal families climbing past every omega^(n+2) in the two blocks under their caps. Weighted canonical execution mass equals voidCost plus remaining-counter times deltaCost plus recDeltaCost plus performed apps times appCost, pointwise orbit equality holds under 0<k together with appCost equal to twice deltaCost with uniform-cost failure past the start, and the same constant profile is shared with a non-well-founded two-cycle. All root bounds need guarded hypotheses, contextual certification needs separate fuel after an exhibited increase under integrate, payload-recursive obstructions defeat all monotone stacks over four coordinates, and the realized trace image stays a proper part of the calibrated carrier with collisions and unrealized phase-one zero-DM points.
boundary: Guarded SafeStep strictly lowers the computable triple measure and its ordinal code below omega-omega times two under epsilon-zero, giving a well-founded reverse with linear root and single-exponential contextual envelopes, while the same root code rises on an exhibited contextual step under integrate so no universal root drop certifies full contexts and the bound must package fuel separately. The obstruction is marked by a concrete source-target pair with rising triple-lex measure, a payload-recursive family defeating every monotone arithmetic and lexicographic stack over four candidate coordinates, and a duplicating recursor with no direct additive whole-term witness although imported-whole and transformed-call witnesses remain. The location is fixed by bidirectional DM and triple-lex correspondences with upper bounds and surjectivity at omega-omega and omega-omega times two, cofinal tower families in both blocks, and a factor-two calibration separating matching from nonmatching mass profiles together with non-surjectivity and collision limits on the full carrier.

conclusions.statement: For all traces t and u and all n, if SafeStepCtxPow n t u then n + 1 is at most 2^(2*termSize t).

On the full binary-phase carrier, Lex3c order holds if and only if the triple-lex ordinal codes are ordered, every code is below omega-omega times two, and every ordinal below omega-omega times two is a code.
DM holds between multisets if and only if their DM ordinal embeddings are ordered, every embedding is below omega-omega, and every ordinal below omega-omega is an embedding.
For every trace t, lex3cToOrd (mu3c t) is below epsilon-zero, and for all a and b with SafeStep a b, lex3cToOrd (mu3c b) is below lex3cToOrd (mu3c a).
For all traces a and b, if SafeStep a b then Lex3c (mu3c b) (mu3c a), and SafeStepRev is well-founded.
For every n, SafeStepCtxPow (ctxLowerLen n) (ctxLowerFamily n) (ctxLowerNF n) holds and 2^n is at most ctxLowerLen n.
For all traces t and u and all n, if SafeStepPow t n u then n + 2 is at most 2*termSize t.
For all t, u and n, if SafeStepCtxPow n t u then n is at most ctxDupPotential t, and for every trace t, ctxDupPotential t + 1 is at most 2^(2*termSize t).
For every n, omega^(n+2) is at most lex3cToOrd (mu3c (payloadTower n)) below omega-omega, and omega-omega plus omega^(n+2) is at most lex3cToOrd (mu3c (flaggedTower n)) below omega-omega times two.
For every weighted algebra A, traces b and s, k and index i in Fin (k+1), the mass of canonicalExecution equals A.voidCost plus (k - i.val)*A.deltaCost plus A.recDeltaCost plus i.val*A.appCost.
For every weighted algebra A, traces b and s and k with 0 < k, pointwise equality of the two orbit mass profiles at all indices holds if and only if A.appCost equals 2*A.deltaCost.

For every uniform-cost algebra A, traces b, s, k and every observer of the complete finite mass profile, the observer takes equal values on the terminating canonical execution and the mass-matched circular orbit prefix, while the two-edge circular comparison relation is not well-founded.
It is false that every SafeStepCtx step has target mu3c below source mu3c in Lex3c, and the exhibited obstruction source to target has target triple-lex measure above source measure.
For every list of coordinate expressions es and every index k, lexicographic stack certification does not hold for the kth payload-family obstruction.

Every primitive-recursor configuration is a structurally incomplete member, the linear complete member with a direct additive witness, or the duplicating complete member with no direct additive witness but with imported-whole and transformed-call witnesses.

openPoints: Guarded root decrease, linear root bounds and tau-based Cichon bounds need SafeStep or SafeStepPow hypotheses; full context-closed StepCtxFull needs separate fuel, envelope and MW bounds.
Single-exponential contextual envelope 2^(2*n) refines the tower bound and is matched below by a linear-size family with length above 2^n and exponential-size outputs, without a machine-model claim.

Pointwise orbit mass equality needs 0<k and appCost equal to twice deltaCost; the uniform-cost instance shows failure past the initial stage, and mass-profile observers give equal values on terminating execution and nonterminating two-cycle.

Realized trace image is a proper part of the calibrated carrier: phase-one points carry 1 in the DM component, phase-one zero-DM carriers have no trace preimage, and distinct traces collide so the carrier map is neither injective nor surjective and no unconditional full-carrier order-type package exists.

No monotone arithmetic expression or lexicographic stack over copy budget, counter budget, tau and copy mass certifies the payload-recursive rec-succ family; relaxed below-approximant descent has no Cichon bound because same-control monotonicity fails, with cichon 5 at 1 equal to 5 exceeding cichon omegaNote at 1 equal to 3.

files.summary: Classifies the six-member family generated by presence or absence of a base rule and absent, linear or duplicating step on RecCore terms. Proves the full linear member has an explicit direct additive witness while any duplicating member has none. Shows duplicating members still have an imported quadratic whole witness and a transformed call witness, giving a complete finite classification.
files.conclusion: Among structurally complete members, full duplicating is the unique one with no direct additive witness but with imported and transformed witnesses.

files.summary: Packages generic right-duplicating recursor witness facts into a canonical witness structure. Instantiates it for KO7 via the role-aware adapter and for textbook, tagged-binary and depth-counter recursors. Connects the KO7 witness to the kernel R_rec_succ step by projection.
files.conclusion: KO7 and three non-KO7 recursors share one canonical witness interface with KO7 projecting to the live kernel step.

files.summary: The file defines a computable Nat rank tau, the Dershowitz-Manna order DM, inner and outer lexicographic orders, and the triple measure mu3c from deltaFlag, kappaM and tau. It proves each of the eight SafeStep constructors strictly decreases mu3c, with delta-drop, multiset-drop or tau-drop. A generic pullback wrapper turns the decrease into well-foundedness of SafeStepRev.
files.conclusion: Every SafeStep step strictly decreases the computable triple measure, so SafeStepRev is well-founded.

files.summary: The file re-checks tau monotonicity, delta transparency and the eq_diff inequality, well-foundedness of Lex3c and DM lifting. It re-checks all eight rule decreases, nested and large-trace edge cases, and the deltaFlag binary and characterization facts. It aggregates to SafeStep decrease, re-checks SafeStepRev well-foundedness, its computable-only derivation, and derives no infinite SafeStep chain.
files.conclusion: All eight rules lower the computable triple measure, so SafeStepRev is well-founded and no infinite SafeStep chain exists.

files.summary: This file gives the positive outcome of the contextual copy-budget complexity program. It defines the syntactic control copyBudget monotone under safe and contextual steps and the position-aware multiplicity potential ctxDupPotential. It proves strict contextual decrease, an exact-length bound by ctxDupPotential, and a single-exponential bound in structural term size.
files.conclusion: Every SafeStepCtx chain from t has length at most ctxDupPotential t and hence at most 2^(2*termSize t) minus one steps.

files.summary: This companion module records obstructions for contextual SafeStepCtx measures. It defines the rejected coordinates counterBudget and copyMass and concrete SafeStep and SafeStepCtx counterexamples where normalization cost, tau or mass increase while copyBudget stays flat. It defines the monotone expression class CoordExpr with lex-stack certification and proves no stack certifies the payload-recursive rec_succ obstruction, uniformly over a Nat-indexed family.
files.conclusion: Every monotone arithmetic expression and every lexicographic stack over the four candidate coordinates fails on the payload-recursive rec_succ family.

files.summary: This module calibrates the DM-based safe measure in ordinals. It defines dmOrdEmbed as a sorted sum of omega powers with inner and outer lex embeddings and unconditional DM and Lex3c ranks. It proves strict monotonicity and order reflection for dmOrdEmbed with bounds below omega^omega and below omega^omega times two and epsilon-zero. It proves strict safe-step decrease both explicitly per rule and via rank, combining rank termination with epsilon-zero calibration.
files.conclusion: Safe steps strictly decrease both the explicit triple ordinal below epsilon-zero and the unconditional Lex3c rank.

files.summary: This file builds a canonical finite CNF payload type for ordinals below ω^ω with conversions to and from multisets and ordinal evaluation through dmOrdEmbed. It proves every code lies below ω^ω and, using Mathlib Cantor normal form decomposition, that every ordinal below ω^ω is hit. It proves reflection of order into DM yields equality of dmOrdEmbed and dmRankOrd, plus injectivity, an order-equivalence package, and a ω^ω·2 bound for the triple-lex measure.
files.conclusion: The DM embedding has exact order type ω^ω with order equivalence, upper bound, surjectivity, injectivity, and equality with dmRankOrd.

files.summary: This file proves the calibrated binary-phase triple-lex image is exactly the ordinals below ω^ω·2. It introduces reflection and injectivity propositions, derives inner LexDM reflection and order equivalence conditionally on DM-code injectivity, then unconditionally. It proves injectivity and equality criteria for inner and carrier codes and packages strict monotonicity, the upper bound, and surjectivity.
files.conclusion: The calibrated binary-phase triple-lex code has exact order type ω^ω·2 with order equivalence, upper bound, and surjectivity.

files.summary: This file packages the final paper-facing catalog for the calibrated binary-phase triple-lex surface as a single structure. It proves the catalog holds after the DM-code injectivity bridge is closed, with no new assumptions. It then projects DM-code injectivity, inner and carrier equality criteria, carrier injectivity, and the exact order-type package.
files.conclusion: The DM-code injectivity bridge closes the full unconditional triple-lex exactness catalog.

files.summary: This file defines the calibrated binary-phase carrier behind the explicit triple-lex image and its forgetful map to Lex3c tuples. It proves every calibrated code lies below ω^ω·2 and that the phase-0 slice is the inner lexDMToOrd block. It proves the inner block is surjective below ω^ω and builds explicit phase-0 and phase-1 families witnessing both ω^ω blocks in the image.
files.conclusion: The binary-phase carrier realizes every ordinal below ω^ω·2 as a triple-lex code.

files.summary: This module is a forwarding surface for the imported DM order-type declarations, with comments describing exports without release claims. It defines a compact upstreamable proposition conjoining order equivalence, boundedness, and surjectivity. It proves that proposition holds and forwards monotonicity, reflection, injectivity, boundedness, and the exact-type package under a staging namespace.
files.conclusion: The repository already proves the full general DM order-type surface claimed upstreamable.

files.summary: The file packages the terminal record family as a first-class externalized-trace object. It defines externalized storage with exact code-decode recovery, the observed image carrier, index-image equivalence, and reusable content-summary packages. It instantiates the package for record-emission witnesses and faithful emitters, including free-syntax packages.
files.conclusion: Terminal record families form reusable externalized-trace packages with exact recovery and index-image equivalence.

files.summary: The file provides the free term algebra for base, succ, wrap and recur as the canonical genuinely generated carrier. It defines counter depth, projection rank and confession-core witness on that syntax. It proves every projection rank and every core witness on the free syntax equals the canonical one by generatedness.
files.conclusion: The free step-duplicating syntax is generated by its constructors with a unique canonical counter-depth rank and core witness.

files.summary: The file embeds free step-duplicating syntax into KO7 Trace and defines partial erasure rejecting non-schema constructors. It proves round-trip exactness and injectivity on the primitive fragment. It builds the primitive image shadow as a generated schema and shows all four confession routes factor through free counter depth on the embedding.
files.conclusion: Every rank satisfying the confession-core semantic profile on free syntax recovers all four KO7 confession ranks on the embedded fragment.

files.summary: This file builds descending multiset towers and root-side and flagged trace towers witnessing large mu3c values. It computes their weights, payloads, tau and delta flags and their ordinal embeddings. It proves polynomial omega-power lower bounds inside the delta 0 and delta 1 blocks with matching block caps, giving existential cofinal families for both blocks.
files.conclusion: Both mu3c blocks contain cofinal realized families below their respective caps.

files.summary: Provides generic slow-growing and Cichon hierarchy definitions on ordinal notations below epsilon-zero by well-founded recursion on fundamental sequences. Proves their unfolding equations for successor and limit notations and their values at zero, one and two. The file intentionally makes no connection to KO7 relations.
files.conclusion: Slow-growing and Cichon hierarchies are defined by well-founded recursion on ordinal notations below epsilon-zero.

files.summary: Defines exact controlled descent that must land exactly on the fundamental-sequence approximant, with an endpoint-tracking relation and its length projection. Proves by induction that any such exact chain of length n from o with control k satisfies n at most cichon o k. Notes this does not allow smaller descendants beneath the approximant.
files.conclusion: Every exact fundamental-sequence descent chain has length bounded by the Cichon value.

files.summary: Computes cichon 5 at 1 equals 5 and cichon omega at 1 equals 3 by kernel unfolding to refute same-control monotonicity of cichon in ordinal representation. Defines an exploratory relaxed controlled descent allowing jumps to any notation below the fundamental-sequence approximant. Records that this relaxed route is unsound for the attempted Cichon bound and provides no derivation-length bound.
files.conclusion: Same-control Cichon monotonicity is false, so the relaxed below-approximant route cannot be bounded that way.

files.summary: Packages guarded normalizer-cost results as an explicit decision-cost envelope for reachability to safe normal-form targets. Defines decision cost as counted normalization steps plus one check and proves it coincides with the normalizer-equality test. Proves a certified upper envelope and a linear bound in source size. Realizes matching linear lower and size families through the merge-void chain to void without claiming a machine model.
files.conclusion: Guarded reachability decision cost is linearly bounded above and matched below by an explicit linear family.

files.summary: This file defines the canonical rewrite sequence of the record-emitting schema using counter terms, frame stacks, and a frame-closed step rule. It proves consecutive canonical stages are related by the step rule below the starting counter height. It proves every positive stage both emits a record frame and preserves the recursive generator, and discharges the manuscript dynamic condition from the positional necessity theorem. It also gives the universally quantified duplication form and inhabitation of the first step.
files.conclusion: Every positive stage of the canonical record-emitting sequence carries distinct frame-slot and active-site generator occurrences.

files.summary: This file introduces a minimal first-order RecordTerm language with one generator constructor and enumerates generator-occurrence positions. It defines frame emission and recursive-generator preservation predicates with frame and active position tags. It proves that joint frame presence and active-site presence yields two distinct generator positions, with a no-record contrapositive and a primitive-duplicator witness.
files.conclusion: Frame emission together with generator preservation forces two syntactically distinct generator occurrences, one in a frame slot and one at the active site.

files.summary: This file extends the record-emission necessity result from single-sort syntax to three broader regimes. It lifts the theorem to many-sorted families per sort, to externalized traces under a faithful-decoder hypothesis, and to richer semantic regimes under a coherence hypothesis. It packages coverage as a three-way unified classifier discharged by decide.
files.conclusion: Architectural necessity lifts to many-sorted syntax, faithful externalized traces, and coherent richer semantic regimes, covered by an exact three-way classifier.

files.summary: This file studies injective natural-number codes with decoders and strictly increasing normalized codes. It proves codes are injective and normalized codes satisfy an index lower bound by strict monotonicity. It builds terminal and terminal-normalized storage forms from a record-emission witness with identity codes and transfers the lower bound to them.
files.conclusion: Every normalized storage code satisfies the index lower bound, instantiated by the terminal witness with identity code.

files.summary: This file distinguishes the input-varying family RecursorInputFamily from the fixed-source finite execution canonicalExecution obtained from BaseDuplicatingSystem.canonicalTrace. It proves the source identity, stepwise StepStar connectivity under wrap closure, counter descent by one, payload ascent by one, terminal form, and source-to-output reachability. It defines a named projected counter observer and proves it reads the remaining counter and drops by one at each step.
files.conclusion: The fixed-source canonical execution starts from the counter-depth source and reaches the wrapped output with stepwise connections and a projected counter that drops by one.

files.summary: This file packages the Trace recursor with its full contextual KO7 relation as ko7BaseSystem and connects adjacent canonical stages by exact contextual edges. It defines general weighted and uniform constructor-cost algebras and proves exact mass formulas with slopes appCost minus deltaCost and deltaCost respectively. It proves pointwise and profile equality with the self-embedding orbit exactly under the sharp factor-two calibration, proves the uniform-cost equality fails past the initial stage, and exhibits a genuine nonterminating two-cycle with the same constant mass profile.
files.conclusion: Weighted mass of the real canonical execution matches the self-embedding orbit exactly under and only under the factor-two calibration, while uniform mass is constant on the execution and a genuine two-cycle reproduces that constant profile despite nontermination.

files.summary: This file defines direct-measure proof systems, counter traces, the step-duplicating recursor orbit and a merge-chain circular-reference orbit, plus the LinearGrowth predicate. It proves exact linear mass formulas for both orbits under uniform-cost equations and that each profile satisfies LinearGrowth. The headline theorem is that both orbits satisfy LinearGrowth under any conforming direct measure, so whole-term mass shape alone does not separate them.
files.conclusion: Under any uniform-cost direct measure both the recursor orbit and the circular-reference orbit satisfy LinearGrowth, so mass shape alone cannot distinguish them.

files.summary: This file proves arithmetic identities and bounds for cumulative cell and marginal bit costs, including the exact subtraction-free identity and geometric lower bound with sufficient projection width. It defines a partial decoder for schema records and proves correctness and injectivity only for canonical positive-depth orbitState records. It records the zero-depth absence, a concrete rejection witness, and the coexistence of exact decoding with a quadratic confessed-mass lower bound.
files.conclusion: Marginal bit costs satisfy exact and lower-bound identities with sufficient projection width, and canonical positive-depth records decode exactly and injectively while inconsistent records are rejected.

files.summary: This file places the seven-constructor RecursorTerm fold inside a generic proof-carrying AlgebraHom interface with free and target algebras. It proves the fold identifies the closed witness pair whenever the target recR ignores its third input. It defines an explicit syntactic counter projection that separates the witnesses and proves it cannot factor through any such homomorphism or through the fold itself.
files.conclusion: The syntactic counter projection separates the witnesses that every third-ignoring homomorphic fold identifies, so it does not factor through the fold.

files.summary: The file defines an entropy measure whose discarded-information functional is invariant on LinearGrowth mass profiles, the discarded information of an orbit under such a measure, and information equivalence modulo the Dependency Pair projection as equality of discarded information under all such measures and uniform-cost direct-measure systems. It proves that any two LinearGrowth profiles share discarded information and that mass indistinguishability implies the same equality. Its headline theorems state that the step-duplicating primitive recursor orbit and a true circular-reference orbit are information-equivalent modulo the DP projection, with corollaries packaging the same equality under uniform-cost hypotheses and a cost-floor reading. It also records H-equivalence reflexivity for the canonical confession move, the definitional fact that canonical discarded bits are zero, and convergence of the canonical move to itself.
files.conclusion: Under any LinearGrowth-invariant entropy measure and uniform-cost direct-measure system, the step-duplicator recursor orbit and the circular-reference orbit have equal discarded-information values modulo the Dependency Pair projection.

files.summary: This file names the self-embedding circular rule t to delta t, its orbit, and its nontermination properties including absence of normal forms and of strictly decreasing natural measures. It proves the self-embedding mass formula, shared initial state with the recursor orbit, and unconditional pointwise and functional mass-profile identity with identical descent verdicts. It proves the upstream merge-chain orbit never matches the recursor pointwise, explaining why LinearGrowth alone does not give separation failure.
files.conclusion: The recursor and self-embedding orbits share initial state and pointwise mass with identical descent verdicts, while the merge-chain orbit never matches and no natural measure descends on the self-embedding rule.

files.summary: This file replaces three vacuous closure forms with contentful statements resting on pointwise mass identity. It defines a mass-profile licensed quotient that is non-constant yet identifies the recursor and circular orbits. It proves index bijections do not transport termination via the DupDP descent versus self-embedding non-descent contrast. It proves information agreement for every functional without an invariance field, witnessed non-vacuously by a slope functional.
files.conclusion: A non-trivial mass-profile quotient identifies the two orbits, index bijections carry no termination content, and every functional agrees on the two pointwise-identical profiles.

files.summary: This file defines a declared arithmetic payload profile, a counter-index profile, and MassIndistinguishable as the conjunction of two LinearGrowth properties. It proves both declared profiles step by one and, under the displayed normalization equations, that recursor and circular measure sequences each satisfy LinearGrowth. The two concluding theorems state this conjunction, with equality and observational equivalence explicitly outside the definition.
files.conclusion: Under the three normalization equations both the recursor and circular-measure sequences satisfy LinearGrowth and hence MassIndistinguishable.

files.summary: This file defines an r-ary duplicator emitting r payload copies per step with functional steps, orbit states, payload counts and counted derivations. It proves payload multiplicity r*i+1, payload- and r-blind runtime k+1 with uniqueness of normalizing length and endpoint, and exact cumulative mass with a linear scaling envelope. Its architectural section counts generator positions in a constructed multi-frame term without claiming necessity for arbitrary encodings.
files.conclusion: The r-ary duplicator has payload multiplicity r*i+1, unique normalizing runtime k+1, closed cumulative mass with linear scaling envelope, and a constructed multi-frame term with m+1 generator positions.

files.summary: The file defines r-ary analogues of the binary duplicator quantities, scaling wrapper weight to r*w while keeping the single active payload explicit. It proves live-orbit bridges showing the closed sums equal sums over the actual r-orbit and an exact gap formula for naive weight substitution. It proves the six quantitative laws at every arity r, with positivity-dependent clauses stated as implications. It packages all laws with their bridges into one structure inhabited for every r and shows r = 1 recovers the binary statements as equalities.
files.conclusion: Every r-ary quantitative law holds at all arities and the whole package is inhabited for every r with r = 1 recovering the binary laws as equalities.

files.summary: The file defines SigmaAlgebra interpretations for the seven-constructor RecursorTerm signature and the recursive fold evaluator. It proves fold is a Sigma-homomorphism and that any function satisfying the seven homomorphism equations equals the fold. It defines the constant-void algebra and shows folding through it equals dpCollapseToVoid. It defines FactorsThroughCollapse as constancy and proves homomorphisms into constant algebras are constant and hence cannot distinguish terms.
files.conclusion: Any homomorphism into a constant algebra is constant and therefore takes equal values on any two recursor terms.

files.summary: The file defines the SchemaTerm syntax with base and payload leaves and the rewrite relation SStep with root rules and G-context closure. It defines the canonical orbit orbitState and measures wsize, countG, countPay, ctr and hasF. It proves each live state takes a unique canonical next step and the leaf-instantiated terminal record is normal. It proves exact closed forms for size, G-count, payload-count, counter height and frame presence on live and terminal states.
files.conclusion: Every live canonical state steps uniquely along the orbit to a normal terminal record with exact size and count closed forms.

files.summary: The file defines the recursor fragment RecTerm and its Sigma-algebras with a ternary recursor slot. It proves any algebra whose recursor slot is constant in its third argument identifies the two witness terms differing only in that argument. It defines the counter-height algebra that reads the third argument and separates the witnesses while failing the constancy hypothesis. It combines both facts to state non-derivability is relative to the constant-third-argument class.
files.conclusion: Non-derivability holds relative to constant-third-argument evaluators and fails for an evaluator that reads the third argument.

files.summary: The file defines a constant licensed quotient on Nat to Trace and a compatibility predicate requiring equal quotient images plus LinearGrowth of both mass profiles. It proves the recursor and circular-reference orbits satisfy this agreement under three constructor-cost equations and pairs it with independent toy-operator factorization facts. It proves both canonical orbits are injective and builds an index-preserving transport map commuting with the one-step successor, yielding a bidirectional orbit-system isomorphism. It defines the constructor-cost measure satisfying the three equations and instantiates licensed-quotient and information agreement at it.
files.conclusion: The recursor and circular-reference orbits agree under the constant licensed quotient with shared linear growth and are isomorphic as one-step orbit systems, instantiated without open hypotheses at the constructor-cost measure.

files.summary: The file proves base and payload identifiers are never frame-headed in the sorted schema syntax and that the decoder is defined on canonical positive-depth terminal records. It defines an unsorted record syntax without sort separation and its frame stack. It exhibits a depth collision where different depths and bases yield the same terminal record and shows barring frame-headed bases restores depth recoverability.
files.conclusion: The unrestricted total decoder is false without sort separation, while the sorted decoder is total on canonical positive-depth records.

files.summary: The file defines the triangular number tri, the live-trace action traceAction and confession masses conMassCell and conMassPayManuscript. It proves summation bridges and exact division-free closed forms for the syntactic sum, the action and the partition between wrapper-cell and retained mass. It proves integer envelopes for the second quadratic invariant, confession dominance and the manuscript payload mass.
files.conclusion: The live-trace action and confession masses satisfy exact division-free closed forms and partitions with quadratic envelopes.

files.summary: The file defines integer linear and full affine readings of the canonical coordinates trace_ctr, trace_pay and trace_wraps. It proves a functional is conserved along live stages iff k = 0 or a = b+c, with rank-two basis ctr+wraps and pay-wraps and values k and 1. It classifies conserved coefficient vectors, observational equivalence of readings and conserved observations, showing three conserved coefficients collapse to two observable parameters.
files.conclusion: Conservation along a trace holds exactly under coefficient balance a = b+c except for vacuous zero depth, with a rank-two basis and two observable parameters.

files.summary: The file defines multi-step reachability StepsTo and proves determinism gives unique normal lengths and records. It proves Law 1 exact length and payload blindness, Law 2 mass rate and terminal drop, Law 5 crossover envelope and minimality, Laws 6-7 step budget, offset and sufficient-statistic with uniqueness, and Law 11 orbit injectivity and carrier dimension.
files.conclusion: Canonical traces have exact length k+1 with unique normal records, conserved budgets and injectively indexed orbits.

files.summary: This file proves the root tail measure is linear in structural term size and that exact guarded root reductions are linearly bounded and lift to context-closed chains. It shows the counted root normalizer length is realized by an exact path and therefore bounded by computable fuel, the size-based tower bound, the MW root bound and a linear size bound. It restates the merge-spine exact lower bound to give matching linear lower and size families.
files.conclusion: The certified root normalizer runs in linear term size with a matching linear lower family.

files.summary: This file attaches the proved single-exponential SafeStepCtx bound to a finite note and its Cichon value. It proves the note denotes exactly the exponential bound and lies below ω, hence the bound is below its Cichon value. It concludes that every exact contextual chain length is bounded by that Cichon value, with a paper-facing alias of the same statement.

files.summary: This file studies diagonal wrapper stacks with seed-rank, maximum and additive coordinates, proving they coincide degenerately but separate strictly for i at least 2 and p at least 2 while maximum is always at most additive and seed rank needs positive size. It defines stipulated logarithmic gauge entropies and a quadratic-over-log inefficiency coefficient, proving linear lower bounds, unboundedness and Theta characterizations for direct, per-residual and per-step rates. It also defines repeated-carrier mass and explicit description length, proving a logarithmic upper bound, an exact balance identity and its linear-gap rearrangement.

files.summary: This file mechanizes wrapper cells, stacks and payload tuples for base duplicating systems, proving stack length, diagonal entries and offset conservation against the payload coordinate. It proves permutation gauge symmetry where constant tuples are fixed by every payload permutation and additive mass is permutation-invariant while recording multiplicity exactly and strictly increasingly for positive size. It proves the counter is the unique gauge-invariant retained coordinate that strictly descends and reverses, whereas payload and wrap multiplicities ascend.

files.summary: Defines diagonal submodules, collapse maps forgetting carrier multiplicity, and families of payload observables. Proves a payload family is insensitive to carrier multiplicity along the diagonal if and only if it factors through the collapse maps, with a unique factoring map.
